verdict.rationale: ADK ships its own CLI that runs agents from a terminal (`adk run path/to/my_agent`). Its `adk eval` command runs bundled sample agents (e.g. samples_for_testing/hello_world, contributing/samples/evaluation/home_automation_agent) against evalset files, which gives a terminal-driven way to check agent behavior. The evidence does not show that `adk run` works non-interactively (piped input, machine-readable output, exit codes), so whether an AI agent can fully script it headlessly is unproven. missing for 10: documented non-interactive/scriptable mode for `adk run` (stdin input, structured output, exit codes), explicit docs on running the shipped example agents headlessly for agent self-verification, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can run the framework's example agents headlessly from a terminal so an agent can verify what it just built

citations.quote: It's most effective during active agent development, serving as a form of unit testing.
